International Seminar
(January 08-09, 2027)
ICT for Research, Extension, Entrepreneurship and Development
(ICT4REED)
: - Invitation: -
Dear Sir/Madam,
It is my proud privilege to inform that Department of Agricultural Extension Education, Faculty
of Agriculture, Birsa Agricultural University, Ranchi and Centre for Development of Advanced
Computing (C-DAC), Kolkata are jointly organizing International Seminar on “ICT for Research,
Extension, Entrepreneurship and Development” in collaboration with National Bank for Agriculture and
Rural Development (NABARD), Ranchi on January 08-09, 2027.
Your kind participation and valuable contribution in the form of paper, technology/ product
display and deliberations will be of great help towards the success of the programme. The event is
expected to be an effective interface between innovators, knowledge workers, industry and farmer users.
The deliberations will be compiled in the form of proceedings which will be submitted to relevant
stakeholders for promotion and application.
It is proposed to bring out souvenir–cum-compendium of abstract at the time of seminar. Selected
full length paper will be published in the proceedings.
Looking forward to your gracious presence and participation.
With kind regards,
Yours Sincerely,
Sd/
(S.C. Dubey)
Vice Chancellor, BAU, Ranchi
ICT for Research, Extension, Entrepreneurship and Development (ICT4REED)
ICT application has moved from information dissemination to transactional services and system
automation. The recent advances in the field of Artificial Intelligence, ROBOTICS including Drone,
Block Chain Technology, Big Data Analytics and Internet of Things have been slowly entering into social,
economic, psychological and political sphere of human civilization. Social media has transformed
communication and inter-personal relations. Agriculture being the primary occupation has also started to
experience the touch of these advanced ICT applications. Organizations across the globe have been trying
to promote these technologies into the field of farmers. Considering the socio -economic significance of
ICT in all its advanced form, Department of Agricultural Extension Education, Faculty of Agriculture,
Birsa Agricultural University (BAU), Ranchi is organizing International Seminar on “ICT for Research,
Extension, Entrepreneurship and Development” in collaboration with Centre for Development of
Advanced Computing (C-DAC) , Kolkata and National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (
NABARD), Ranchi on the following themes :
1. Digital Extension and Advisory Services for Crop, Livestock and Horticultural Systems: Mobile
advisory, farmer helplines, e-extension portals and chatbot advisory, crop calendars and agronomy
advisories, horticultural production and post-harvest guidance, livestock and animal husbandry advice,
fisheries, and veterinary helplines.
2. Data, AI and Decision Support for Research and Extension: Big data, remote sensing, IoT and
sensor networks, AI/ML models for forecasting, surveillance and precision advisories. Agronomic and
soil-crop modelling, soil health and fertility mapping, digital soil spectroscopy, plant genetics and
genomics, breeding informatics, genotyping platforms, marker-assisted and genomic selection decision
tools, phenotyping and phenomics, horticultural crop modelling, livestock performance and herd-health
analytics, and agri-engineering applications like machine vision for quality grading, sensor-driven
irrigation, mechanisation telemetry.
3. Digital Entrepreneurship and Agribusiness Platforms: Digital marketplaces, e-commerce for inputs
and produce, aggregator and logistics platforms, fintech and index-based insurance, and the gig economy
in agri-services. Horticultural value chains and cold-chain platforms, seed and nursery trade, agro-input
retail, feed and fodder markets, livestock and dairy marketing, animal health service delivery, custom
hiring centres, machinery rental and repair networks.
4. Capacity Building, Digital Literacy and Inclusive Access: Training researchers, extension agents,
students and farmers in digital skills; access for women, youth and marginalized groups; assistive and
low-literacy interfaces; language and localization. Capacity building of faculty and students in data
science, bioinformatics, GIS and modelling skills, and digital pedagogy for laboratory, field and clinical
teaching.
5. ICT-Enabled Rural Development, Governance and Public Services: Digital public infrastructure
for agriculture and allied sectors, e-governance for entitlements, community information centres,
community-radio-plus-digital hybrids, and ICT for health, education and financial inclusion in rural areas.
One Health and zoonoses surveillance, veterinary service delivery and animal traceability, soil and land
governance records, natural resource and watershed monitoring, water accounting, and rural sanitation
and nutrition programmes.
6. Enabling Environment for ICT Application: Policy, Standards, Infrastructure and Sustainability
Data governance and farmer data ownership, privacy and consent, interoperability standards, spectrum
and connectivity policy, and the economics of sustaining digital services after donor funding ends.
Genetic-resource and data-sharing policy, access and benefit sharing, germplasm and genomic data
sovereignty, biosafety and regulatory dimensions of new breeding technologies, soil and land data
standards, instrumentation and equipment standards in agri-engineering, animal health data and
traceability standards, e-waste, and the environmental and energy footprint of digital agriculture.
7. Evidence, Impact and Scaling: M&E, Partnerships and Business Models, Rigorous evaluation of
ICT4REED interventions, RCTs, quasi-experimental designs, cost-effectiveness, metrics for adoption and
behaviour change, and pathways from pilot to scale. Multi-stakeholder partnerships, public–private
models, and lessons from failure. Yield and input-use efficiency, soil health and fertility change,
horticultural quality and shelf life, genetic gain and breeding-cycle time, livestock productivity, health
and welfare, mechanisation access and drudgery reduction, and environmental outcomes.
Participants
Participants will include teachers, scientists, research scholars, engineers, farm innovators, agripreneurs,
officials of line departments, representatives of IT companies and non-government organizations.
Call for papers
The participants may submit their abstract (not exceeding 300 words) and full-length paper (not exceeding
5000 words) in Times New Roman 12 font size and 1.5 spacing.
Submission of abstract:25th December, 2026
Submission of full-length paper: 31st December, 2026
Presentation Award & Recognition
Participants whose abstracts have been selected will be invited for oral or poster presentation. Best oral
and poster will be awarded in each theme with certificate and memento.
